gap: No result ChatGPT got lines up the three makers' 'AVR' and 'noise filtering' claims on one scale: CyberPower's own spec lists its AVR as 'Single Boost' (it raises low voltage but lists no buck/trim step) and gives only 'EMI/RFI Filtration: Yes' with no dB or let-through figure. So the pick ChatGPT named 'Best overall' for 'power conditioning' has the least specific conditioning spec of the three, and only the CyberPower side of that comparison could be sourced from a page I opened.
standout_why: Rival result 5 (cyberpower.com global CP1500PFCLCDa page) already states 'Single Boost', 88–144 V input and 'EMI/RFI Filtration: Yes', so the raw CyberPower facts are already in ChatGPT's results. What none of the results do is set those next to APC's boost+trim and stated let-through figure and Tripp Lite's AVR window as one comparison. I could not open a maker page or datasheet for APC SMT1500C or Tripp Lite SMART1500LCDT to source that comparison. eaton.com timed out three times, the se.com product page returned 503 twice, apc.com redirected to a brand page, the B&H, Micro Center, Newegg and Provantage pages returned 403, and every datasheet PDF (surveillance-video, squarespace, Newegg, blueally, Mouser) came back as unreadable compressed binary. So the comparison that would stand out is not sourced, and the part that is sourced is already in a rival result.
decides: If it can be sourced, it confirms ChatGPT's closing caveat and sharpens it: for a shopper who asked specifically for a 'power conditioner', CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD's 'AVR' only boosts low voltage, and its filtering is a yes/no claim with no number. That weakens calling it 'Best overall' for conditioning, though it is still the pure-sine pick on price. As it stands I can't change the pick, because the APC and Tripp Lite figures that would decide it come only from search snippets.

findings.label: Automatic Voltage Regulation type
findings.note: Maker's spec table lists AVR as 'Single Boost'. No buck/trim step is listed. This is the global 'a' SKU page; the US CP1500PFCLCD page (cyberpowersystems.com) returned HTTP 405, so US-SKU parity is assumed, not verified.

findings.label: Input voltage range
findings.note: Listed as 'Input Voltage Range (Vac) 88 ~ 144'. The page does not say whether this is the AVR window or the transfer-to-battery window.

findings.label: Output voltage regulation
findings.value: 120 V ±5% (stated for on-battery; header 'Output Voltage' also 120 V ±5%)
findings.note: The 'Nominal Output Voltage' field is blank, and no separate line/AVR-mode regulation band is given. ±5% of 120 V = 114–126 V.

findings.label: Noise filtering spec
findings.value: EMI/RFI Filtration: Yes (no dB attenuation or let-through figure stated)

findings.label: Waveform on battery / transfer time
findings.value: Pure sine wave; 4 ms typical transfer

findings.label: Capacity and runtime
findings.value: 1,500 VA / 1,000 W; 10 min at half load, 2.5 min at full load
findings.note: Maker spec table; half load = 500 W, full load = 1,000 W.
